quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The phrasal verb after "I'll" tells you what the speaker will do.
quests.explanation: Look into means to investigate and look for means to search for something. One sounds like a promise to solve, the other like a hunt.
quests.prompt: I'll look into the problem and get back to you before the end of the day.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll look for the problem and get back to you before the end of the day.
quests.followUpQuestion: Promise to look into a problem, and say when you will report back.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A two-word verb starts the sentence. What does it mean?
quests.explanation: No change. "Find out" means to discover information, and it fits with an indirect question.
quests.prompt: We need to find out what time the last train leaves before we make plans.
quests.sampleAnswer: We need to find out what time the last train leaves before we make plans.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you would need to find out before making plans.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A request uses a phrasal verb with an object in the middle.
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. The object "the children" goes between "drop" and "off", because it's a noun phrase.
quests.prompt: Could you drop the children off at school on your way to work?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you drop the children off at school on your way to work?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask someone to take the children somewhere, and say when.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A small problem and its consequence are joined by "so".
quests.explanation: "Run out of" means that the supply is finished, and it is followed by the noun.
quests.prompt: I ran out of milk this morning, so I had to make black coffee.
quests.sampleAnswer: I ran out of milk this morning, so I had to make black coffee.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what happened when you ran out of something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One phrasal verb tells you whether the launch is postponed or cancelled.
quests.explanation: Put off means to delay until later, and call off means to cancel. If you hear the second, the launch might never happen.
quests.prompt: The company has decided to call off the launch for a few months.
quests.sampleAnswer: The company has decided to put off the launch for a few months.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain the difference between putting off and calling off, with an example.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A ride is offered. Are you being collected or taken somewhere?
quests.explanation: Pick up and drop off are opposite parts of a lift. A friend would wait at home in one case and at the cinema in the other.
quests.prompt: I'll pick you up outside the cinema at seven, if that works for you.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll drop you off outside the cinema at seven, if that works for you.
quests.followUpQuestion: Offer someone a lift and say where you will meet.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A small word after "checking" sets the direction of the stay.
quests.explanation: In means arriving at the hotel, and out means leaving it. Both connect with leaving bags, so only your ear knows the difference.
quests.prompt: We're checking in at two, so we can leave our bags at the desk.
quests.sampleAnswer: We're checking out at two, so we can leave our bags at the desk.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain what happens when you check in at a hotel.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two phrasal verbs appear in one sentence. Match them to their objects.
quests.explanation: "Work out" means to figure out a solution, and "set up" means to prepare for use.
quests.prompt: It took us a while to work out how to set up the printer.
quests.sampleAnswer: It took us a while to work out how to set up the printer.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe something you worked out on your own.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A request to a customer. The first phrasal verb is what the customer has to do.
quests.explanation: Filling in means writing on the form, and handing in means giving it to someone. The customer would do a different action.
quests.prompt: Could you hand in this form while I sort out the details of your booking?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you fill in this form while I sort out the details of your booking?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a customer to do a task while you do another.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A deal is offered between two people. Track both halves.
quests.explanation: Nothing was altered in this one. "Look after" means to take care of, and "cover for" means to do someone's job when they're away.
quests.prompt: If you look after the kids tonight, I'll cover for you next weekend.
quests.sampleAnswer: If you look after the kids tonight, I'll cover for you next weekend.
quests.followUpQuestion: Offer to swap a favour with a friend, using cover for.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The problem is stated, then the solution. Focus on who was called.
quests.explanation: A mechanic and a tow truck are both sensible, but they solve the problem in different ways.
quests.prompt: My car broke down on the motorway, so I had to call a mechanic.
quests.sampleAnswer: My car broke down on the motorway, so I had to call a tow truck.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you would do if your car broke down on the way to work.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The advice includes a verb that tells you how much sugar is allowed.
quests.explanation: Cut out means to stop completely and cut down on means to reduce. The patient would eat a lot differently.
quests.prompt: The doctor advised me to cut out sugar and get more sleep.
quests.sampleAnswer: The doctor advised me to cut down on sugar and get more sleep.
quests.followUpQuestion: Give a friend some advice about eating or sleeping.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A common workplace promise, with a condition of timing.
quests.explanation: "Get back to" means to reply after checking, and "as soon as" sets the timing.
quests.prompt: I'll get back to you as soon as I've checked with the team.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll get back to you as soon as I've checked with the team.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell someone you will reply once you have checked something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A phrasal verb tells you how the idea appeared.
quests.explanation: Text and audio are the same. "Came up with" means she thought of it, and "while" gives the situation.
quests.prompt: She came up with a brilliant idea while we were stuck in traffic.
quests.sampleAnswer: She came up with a brilliant idea while we were stuck in traffic.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe a good idea you came up with in an unusual place.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A teacher gives an instruction with a deadline and a reason. Listen to the reason.
quests.explanation: Marking means checking the work, and returning means giving it back. Students would expect a different result over the weekend.
quests.prompt: Please hand in your assignments by Friday so I can mark them over the weekend.
quests.sampleAnswer: Please hand in your assignments by Friday so I can return them over the weekend.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell a group how and when to submit their work.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The verb in the middle introduces a fact.
quests.explanation: "Pointed out" means to draw attention to something that people may not have noticed.
quests.prompt: The manager pointed out that we've been over budget for three months.
quests.sampleAnswer: The manager pointed out that we've been over budget for three months.
quests.followUpQuestion: Point out a problem politely to a colleague.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two phrasal verbs with "up" are easy to confuse. Which is it?
quests.explanation: Keep up means to stay at the same pace, and catch up means to get to the same level after falling behind.
quests.prompt: I've been trying to catch up with the news, but there's too much.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've been trying to keep up with the news, but there's too much.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you try to stay up to date with.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A plan is mentioned, then dropped. Track the verb after "going to".
quests.explanation: The recording follows the text word for word. "Bring up" means to raise a subject for discussion.
quests.prompt: He was going to bring up the problem at the meeting, but he changed his mind.
quests.sampleAnswer: He was going to bring up the problem at the meeting, but he changed his mind.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something you had planned to bring up, and why you didn't.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The reason is in the first half and uses a phrasal verb.
quests.explanation: One bus stopped working, the other never arrived. Either way you walk, but the story about the delay is not the same.
quests.prompt: The bus broke down, so we had to walk the whole way home.
quests.sampleAnswer: The bus didn't turn up, so we had to walk the whole way home.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain how you got home when transport failed.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two verbs show who gives and who receives.
quests.explanation: Taking over and handing over are opposites. One team gains the work while the other loses it.
quests.prompt: Our team is handing over the project to the design department next month.
quests.sampleAnswer: Our team is taking over the project from the design department next month.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what your team will hand over or take over next month.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Surprise is expressed and an action is described.
quests.explanation: "Gave up" means she stopped doing it, and the infinitive shows her purpose.
quests.prompt: I can't believe she gave up her job to travel around the world.
quests.sampleAnswer: I can't believe she gave up her job to travel around the world.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what someone you know gave up, and what you think of it.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One friend prepares the room, and you can hear what kind of preparation.
quests.explanation: Setting up means getting things ready before the meeting, and cleaning up means tidying after it. The timing of the job is different.
quests.prompt: I'll clean up the meeting room while you prepare the slides.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll set up the meeting room while you prepare the slides.
quests.followUpQuestion: Share out two jobs before an event between you and a friend.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An unexpected result is signalled by "ended up".
quests.explanation: The audio matches the text. "Ended up" describes the final result of a series of events.
quests.prompt: We ended up eating at home because every restaurant was fully booked.
quests.sampleAnswer: We ended up eating at home because every restaurant was fully booked.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say where you ended up last time your plans changed.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A habit explains a reaction. Follow the words "used to".
quests.explanation: "Used to" plus -ing means she's accustomed to it, and it differs from the past habit "used to" plus a bare verb.
quests.prompt: She's used to getting up early, so the early flight doesn't bother her.
quests.sampleAnswer: She's used to getting up early, so the early flight doesn't bother her.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you are used to doing every day.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two contrasting ideas are separated by "but".
quests.explanation: This is a straight match. "Looking forward to" is followed by -ing, and "might" shows uncertainty.
quests.prompt: I'm looking forward to seeing you, but I might be late because of work.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm looking forward to seeing you, but I might be late because of work.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you are looking forward to, and what might get in the way.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The picnic's future is decided by a phrasal verb.
quests.explanation: Put off keeps the picnic alive for another day, while call off cancels it. It's a common source of confusion.
quests.prompt: They put off the picnic because it was pouring with rain.
quests.sampleAnswer: They called off the picnic because it was pouring with rain.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you would do if a plan fell through because of the weather.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Advice with two actions. Hear both verbs.
quests.explanation: "Run into" means to meet unexpectedly, and "give me a call" is an informal request.
quests.prompt: If you run into any problems, just give me a call and I'll help.
quests.sampleAnswer: If you run into any problems, just give me a call and I'll help.
quests.followUpQuestion: Offer help to a colleague who might run into difficulties.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A journey is interrupted. Follow the order of verbs.
quests.explanation: "Set off" starts the trip, and "turned back" reverses it.
quests.prompt: After we set off, we realised we'd forgotten the tickets, so we turned back.
quests.sampleAnswer: After we set off, we realised we'd forgotten the tickets, so we turned back.
quests.followUpQuestion: Retell the trip, starting with "We set off, but..."

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A struggle with a habit at a certain time of day.
quests.explanation: Morning and evening cravings are about different routines, like coffee and dessert.
quests.prompt: I'm trying to give up sugar, but it's really hard in the evenings.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm trying to give up sugar, but it's really hard in the mornings.
quests.followUpQuestion: Talk about a habit you are trying to give up.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The result of a long meeting is described in the last words.
quests.explanation: Anything means nothing was agreed, whereas a date means only one issue was left open.
quests.prompt: The meeting dragged on for hours, and nobody could agree on a date.
quests.sampleAnswer: The meeting dragged on for hours, and nobody could agree on anything.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe a meeting that dragged on, and what you would have changed.
